readings: yout_r is cleared to 0 when start is asserted / when i==0, so each multiplication starts from a zero product (required for correct results on back-to-back operations)
yout_r is cleared ONLY by rst_n (the spec only lists reset for areg/breg/yout_r); at i==0 nothing clears it, so a second operation accumulates on top of the previous product and yout is wrong
ambiguities.concrete_effect: yout value for the 2nd and later multiplications differs (correct product vs. sum of both products)

readings: done_r is cleared only when i==17 (or rst_n), so if start is deasserted before i reaches 17 the counter returns to 0 but done stays 1 indefinitely, and a one-cycle start pulse can leave done stuck at 1
done_r is cleared whenever start is inactive or whenever i is reset to 0, so done is low as soon as start is released
ambiguities.concrete_effect: done waveform after start deassertion: stuck high vs. immediately low

readings: start is a level that must remain asserted for all 17 counter steps, because '!start resets i to 0'; a one-cycle start pulse performs no accumulation and yout stays/becomes 0 while done may never assert
start is a one-cycle trigger that latches internal run/busy logic, so a single-cycle pulse completes the whole multiplication with done pulsing later
ambiguities.concrete_effect: given a 1-cycle start pulse, either no product is produced or the full product is produced

readings: areg/breg/yout_r only update while start is active (the load at i==0 is explicitly conditional on start being active), so they hold their values when start is low
areg/breg/yout_r update every clock regardless of start, so ain/bin are continuously captured into areg/breg and yout_r is re-accumulated/driven from live inputs while start is low
ambiguities.concrete_effect: values of areg/breg/yout_r (and hence yout) during cycles where start==0 differ

concrete_effect_note: yout/done cycle-by-cycle behaviour differs between readings
